doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: State of jazz education
summary: Education is good, but mentors and bandstand experience matter most.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Okay. Let’s wrap up with what do you think of the state of jazz education? Do you have an opinion?

I think it’s good because there’s always a new crop of young people that are willing to commit to the journey. And they’re looking to be educated not just in institutions but in the experience of having mentors and real life, you know, experience, gigs. That’s where you really learn. You learn a lot in school as well and I think it’s great when I think of people like Sean Jones you know, now going to Peabody. And I hear the young people playing that are very good you know. So I think we’re in a great space. I don’t like to demonize — everything has its place. The school thing is the structure of school. There’s a lot to be learned there. But as a player, having that experience either as a fly on the wall or if you can actually make it onto the bandstand, being there to see the real thing is the most important as a player.
